brief.headline: Continuity Guardian could not reach its model to produce a grounded review
brief.what_broke: 12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 365398 (batch_worker/adhoc_reporting, idle in transaction, txn open 4.1s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
brief.who_is_affected: Checkout success 0% over 30s (120/120 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $18,400/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

options.description: Terminate the root blocker session (batch_worker/adhoc_reporting, pid 365398) to release its locks.
Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
options.cost: about $18,400/min of checkout revenue at risk while waiting

brief.recommendation: The root blocker pid 365398 has been idle in transaction for only 4.1s (DB-1). Business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout (BIZ-1, BIZ-4). We lack workload registry data (BIZ-2) and trade-off computation is impossible without a registry entry (BIZ-5), making termination risk assessment uncertain. No change-calendar window covers adhoc_reporting (BIZ-3). Waiting allows the blocker to finish naturally within the 60s tolerated window while we gather missing registry data.

audit.report: During the incident an unknown workload (adhoc_reporting) acquired a lock that became the root blocker (pid 365398), causing checkout sessions to wait and time out. Over the 15‑second window after injection, checkout succeeded 33/60 times (55%) with 27 timeouts, and revenue at risk was approximately $4,600 per minute. The Database Guardian recommended waiting because the blocker had been idle in transaction for only 4.1 s and the business tolerates up to 60 s of degraded checkout, but critical data (workload registry entry, change‑calendar window) was missing. The Continuity Guardian could not produce a grounded review, so the matter was escalated to the on‑call team; the proposed terminate action was not executed. As a result the checkout remained degraded and the business was not fully recovered at the time of escalation.
audit.root_cause: The root cause was an unidentified adhoc_reporting workload holding a lock (pid 365398) that blocked checkout sessions, and the guardians lacked workload‑registry and change‑calendar data to assess safe termination.
lessons: Define change‑calendar windows for reporting workloads (e.g., adhoc_reporting) in biz.change_calendar, enabling the guardian to confirm whether terminating falls within an allowed period.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian’s wait decision was reasonable given the 4.1 s blocker age and 60 s tolerance, but the absence of workload‑registry and change‑calendar entries left risk uncertain, forcing escalation. The Continuity Guardian failed to produce a grounded review, so the negotiation ended without a resolved outcome.
follow_ups: Add an entry for adhoc_reporting to biz.workload_registry with owner, estimated cost, and lock‑behavior metadata.
Create a change‑calendar window in biz.change_calendar covering adhoc_reporting’s typical run‑time, noting any maintenance windows.
Run a quick impact re‑evaluation using the newly populated registry to set a concrete termination threshold for future lock‑holder incidents.
